solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Tantrum-thrower Prince, half cut, married to another pop star

indicators.note: cutting something in half lops off its back half, leaving only the front three letters of the name

blocks.note: the pop star Prince, keeping only the first half of his name
the singer Madonna, another one-name pop star

explanation.surface: A gossip item: a temperamental Prince, partly censored, wed to a fellow pop idol.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pop stars are real one-name singers; "married to" just joins them side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima donna is an opera's leading lady, and by extension any vain, temperamental person prone to throwing tantrums.

clue.text: Art of growth restriction, courtesy of Brown, with resistance lacking, is a hit

indicators.note: something lacking is missing, so the resistance letter is dropped from what precedes it
words that are hit get knocked about and come out in a battered new order

blocks.note: BR is the standard abbreviation for brown
R is the symbol for electrical resistance, and it is taken away
a treat courtesy of someone is on them, as in 'drinks are on me'
these two short words are the letters to be knocked about

explanation.surface: A tree-pruning hobby promoted by someone called Brown turns out to be a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown loses its R to leave B, which is placed before the ON that 'courtesy of' supplies; the clue reads 'Brown's courtesy' in the order the answer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonsai is the Japanese art of keeping trees miniature by pruning roots and branches, deliberately restricting their growth.

clue.text: Payees, say, aroused but far from hard

indicators.note: aroused means stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters of these two words are the fodder

explanation.surface: People being paid get excited, though nothing is particularly firm, a double entendre in Private Eye style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' teases a sexual reading after 'aroused', but it simply means difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy-peasy is a childish, rhyming way of saying something is very simple, the opposite of difficult.

clue.text: Olivier made it with Fonda, very briefly!

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut down to its opening letter alone

blocks.note: Henry Fonda was the Hollywood actor, so Fonda points to his first name
just the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A boast that Laurence Olivier worked alongside Fonda in a quick production.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier directed and starred in the 1944 film of Shakespeare's play; Henry Fonda was an American screen star.
explanation.definitionFit: Olivier's wartime film of Shakespeare's history play about Agincourt is one of his best-known productions.

clue.text: Balls possibly getting in an erect state, handled badly

definitions.text: Balls possibly getting in an erect state

blocks.clueFragment: Balls possibly getting in an erect state
blocks.note: first meaning: raised or turned upward, as something tilted up might be
second meaning: botched or messed up, British slang

explanation.walkthrough: 'Balls' is both testicles and, in British slang, a mess (a balls-up), so the first half hints at both senses. To cock something up is to bungle it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocked means tilted upwards, and the British slang verb 'cock up' means to make a mess of a job.

clue.text: (& 25ac.) Boss, one who stuffs game

blocks.note: a boss is a raised knob or stud on a surface such as a shield
one who pokes things in, with a ruder second sense intended

explanation.surface: A rude picture of a womanising employer who stuffs things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like an employer, but it is the ornamental knob; the phrase continues across 25-across.
explanation.definitionFit: Stud poker is a form of poker in which some cards are dealt face up, a card game played for money.

clue.text: Hopper, by the way, provides bird's dropping off place

blocks.note: a kangaroo, the familiar hopper, shortened
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A kangaroo, incidentally, offers a place where birds drop their droppings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping off' suggests bird droppings, but it means falling asleep: a roost is where birds sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A roost is the perch where birds settle down to sleep for the night.

clue.text: Male recruited by working girls, for which a minister is responsible

definitions.text: for which a minister is responsible

indicators.note: someone recruited by a group is taken into its ranks, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: he is the male pronoun
working girls is a euphemism for prostitutes

explanation.surface: A man is taken on by prostitutes, a scandal for some government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: The British government has a Minister for the Arts, so the definition is a fair description rather than a jibe at a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting, music, theatre and the like are a cabinet portfolio in Britain, overseen by an arts minister.

clue.text: Patsy gives head to old lecher, following direction

indicators.note: a piece following another comes after it, so the compass point goes at the front

blocks.note: S, south, is a compass direction
a head or headland is a cape
an 'old goat' is a lecherous old man

explanation.surface: A fall guy performs oral sex on an old lecher, as a satirical magazine might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives head' is the rude decoy; head is simply a headland.
explanation.definitionFit: A patsy is a person made to take the blame for others, exactly what a scapegoat is.

clue.text: Drink decarbonised wine on top of drug

indicators.note: decarbonised means with the carbon taken out, so carbon's symbol is removed from the wine
in a down entry, one piece on top of another sits above it, so the wine comes first

blocks.note: sack is an old word for a dry white wine, as drunk by Falstaff
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drink made of flat wine mixed with something narcotic.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the chemical symbol for carbon, so decarbonising sack leaves SAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sake is the Japanese rice wine, an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Penetrator of more than one hole, meerkat's screwed an unknown quantity

definitions.text: Penetrator of more than one hole

indicators.note: something screwed up is twisted out of shape, so the letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: the eight letters of the word, apostrophe ignored, are the fodder
in algebra x, y and z are unknown quantities

explanation.surface: A smutty tale of a promiscuous meerkat and a mysterious partner.
explanation.walkthrough: The holes are keyholes: one key that opens many locks is a master-key.
explanation.definitionFit: A master-key fits many different locks, so it goes into more than one keyhole.

clue.text: Lecher cosying up to date is not on the level

blocks.note: a rake is a dissolute, womanising man
D is the standard abbreviation for date

explanation.surface: A womaniser getting close to his date is being dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' suggests dishonesty, but here it is literal: a raked stage or seating area slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raked means set at a slope, as theatre stages are, so it is not horizontal.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) So-called leader's crappy mid-term DVD every leader of Republicans ignored

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of the party name
a letter that is ignored is left out of the fodder before it is rearranged
something crappy is a mess, so these letters are messed into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the word is the one taken away
the fifteen letters of these words are the fodder before one is dropped

explanation.surface: A sneer at a sham leader's dreadful election-period video, with all Republicans disregarded.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one R from the fodder before rearranging. Medvedev was Russia's president from 2008 to 2012, widely seen as keeping the seat warm for Putin, hence 'so-called'.
explanation.definitionFit: Medvedev was nominally Russia's head of state while Putin, as prime minister, held real power, making him a leader in name only.

clue.text: see 12ac.
One who's hailed airline getting army out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so these letters are put out of their usual order

blocks.note: Virgin Atlantic is Richard Branson's airline
the four letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrated airline gets its military passengers off the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hail Mary prayer begins 'Hail Mary, full of grace', so she is the one who is hailed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic prayer Ave Maria greets the mother of Jesus with the words 'Hail Mary'.

clue.text: Dicky felt Tess Daly's bottom – sucker!

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for faulty or shaky, so these letters are shaken into a new order
the bottom of a word, in a down entry, is its final letter

blocks.note: the eight letters of these two words are anagram fodder
the last letter of the surname

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal: someone groped the TV presenter Tess Daly, the creep.
explanation.walkthrough: Tess Daly is a presenter of the BBC dance show Strictly Come Dancing. Her final Y joins the fodder before shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse fly of Africa feeds on blood, so it is a bloodsucker, spreading sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Come back one second – it'll be the ruin of you

definitions.text: it'll be the ruin of you

indicators.note: coming back means going the opposite way, so the word for come is read from right to left

blocks.note: come, as a noun, is slang for ejaculate
I is the Roman numeral for one
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A warning to someone tempted to return for a second go: it will destroy you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come back' reads as 'return', but 'Come' is a noun, reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemesis, from the Greek goddess of retribution, is a downfall or the agent that brings someone's ruin.

clue.text: No back: very well hidden in skirt but tits on show in this?

indicators.note: said back means read in the opposite direction, so the word No turns round
a thing hidden in another is put inside it, so these pieces are tucked into the garment

blocks.note: taken as written, then turned round
OK means very well, all right
a mini is a short skirt

explanation.surface: A garment that hides a lot below but leaves the breasts exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: A monokini is a topless one-piece swimsuit: the bottom half covered, the breasts bare.
explanation.definitionFit: A monokini is a swimsuit with only a bottom part, so anyone wearing one goes topless.

clue.text: A non-PC parent's sort of tart?

blocks.note: first meaning: a parent who smacks their children, frowned on as politically incorrect
second meaning: British slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.walkthrough: Literally one who slaps, and in British slang an insulting word for a promiscuous woman, itself not politically correct.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person who hits with an open hand and, as derogatory British slang, a loose woman.

clue.text: Blessed, having to drop histrionics initially, was lax

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it
having to drop something means losing it, so that letter comes off the word for blessed

blocks.note: hallowed means made holy, blessed
the opening letter of the word, which is removed

explanation.surface: A sanctified figure, having to give up dramatics, became slack.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the H from the front of the word for blessed leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed means permitted; one who was lax permitted things that a stricter person would have forbidden.

clue.text: Marginalize a royal cherishing love crap

indicators.note: to cherish is to hold close, so the royal holds the other pieces inside her

blocks.note: Princess Anne is a member of the British royal family
love is nil in tennis, and nil looks like the letter O
tat is cheap, worthless rubbish

explanation.surface: Sidelining a member of the royal family who is fond of romantic nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marginalize' suggests sidelining someone, but it means writing in the margins.
explanation.definitionFit: To annotate is to add notes, typically in the margin of a text, a jokey literal reading of marginalize.

clue.text: Pests taking notes from our versifier on an afterthought

indicators.note: taking something from a word means removing it, so the two musical notes come off the poet's name

blocks.note: E. J. Thribb, aged 17 and a half, is Private Eye's resident spoof poet
B is a musical note, and two of them are removed
PS, postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Nuisances seizing the poet's notebooks and adding a postscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our' signals Private Eye's in-house poet E. J. Thribb, whose obituary verses are a long-running joke in the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrips are tiny winged insects that damage crops and garden plants, a common type of pest.

clue.text: Students once a Scottish smoker gets in pissed

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
lum is a Scots word for chimney, which smokes
the two letters of the word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of former students and a Scottish smoker who turns up drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: The smoker is not a person but a Scottish chimney.
explanation.definitionFit: Alumni are former pupils or graduates of a school or university, people who were students in the past.

clue.text: Woman acting head off, being a cow

indicators.note: with its head off, a word loses its first letter

blocks.note: Mo is a woman's name, short for Maureen
acting means doing something

explanation.surface: A woman playing the decapitation scene in a drama is behaving like a nasty cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being a cow' suggests being spiteful, but it is literal: lowing like cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mooing is the sound a cow makes, so it is what a cow is doing when it acts like one.

clue.text: Lives disrupted by androgynous bird

indicators.note: something disrupted by an intruder is split open, so the other piece goes into the middle

blocks.note: lives means is, exists
bi is short for bisexual, attracted to both sexes

explanation.surface: Lives upset by a gender-ambiguous bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Androgynous strictly means of no clear sex; the setter stretches it to bisexual for BI.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a downcurved bill, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: see 6dn.
Depression time for the PM

blocks.note: a pit is a hollow or depression in the ground
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A gloomy period lies ahead for the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests low spirits or an economic slump, but it is a hole in the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: William Pitt the Elder and his son Pitt the Younger were both British Prime Ministers.

clue.text: Reasonable capacity of bendy bit of member Heath bent back

indicators.note: something bent back is folded the other way, so the word for heath is read from right to left

blocks.note: the joint where an arm, a limb or member, bends
a heath is open moorland

explanation.surface: A rude riddle about the flexible part of a member, with ex-PM Edward Heath bent over backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' tempts a ruder reading, but it is a limb; Heath with a capital looks like the Prime Minister, but it is open land.
explanation.definitionFit: Elbow room is enough space to move about freely, a comfortable amount of capacity.

clue.text: Camp types erection aids

blocks.note: surface reading: effeminate men providing assistance with sexual arousal
setter's reading: kinds of equipment used at a campsite to put up shelters

explanation.walkthrough: Camp here is a campsite, not flamboyance, and the erection is that of a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent-poles are the rods that hold up a tent, so they help with putting it up when camping.

clue.text: Some tosser whose deposit is frozen?

definitions.text: Some tosser whose deposit is frozen?

blocks.clueFragment: Some tosser whose deposit is frozen?
blocks.note: surface reading: an idiot whose bank savings have been blocked

blocks.clueFragment: Some tosser whose deposit is frozen?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a man who masturbates to provide sperm that a clinic stores frozen

explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for an idiot and literally a masturbator; a frozen deposit sounds like a blocked bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: A sperm donor gives a sample that a clinic freezes and stores for later fertility treatment.
